patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.chiefComplaint: Fever and pain behind my eyes
presentation.quote: I'm visiting from Malaysia. Three days ago the fever hit all at once, then the headache behind my eyes and every bone started aching. I feel nauseated, but I haven't had any bleeding or bad stomach pain.
presentation.triageNote: 34-year-old male visitor from Malaysia with three days of abrupt high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgia, nausea and a faint macular rash, without bleeding, severe abdominal pain or persistent vomiting.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 4 is appropriate because this stable suspected dengue presentation without warning signs is expected to require one laboratory resource category and hydration assessment.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This traveler has an uncomplicated dengue-like febrile syndrome without bleeding, severe abdominal pain, shock, or persistent vomiting.
clinical.acuityReason: This stable suspected dengue presentation without warning signs is expected to require one laboratory resource category and hydration assessment.
keyFindings: Three days of abrupt high fever
No bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or persistent vomiting
teachingPoints: Abrupt fever, severe retro-orbital pain, myalgia and rash after time in a dengue-endemic region support dengue. He is stable and has no warning signs, so outpatient management after one laboratory resource category and hydration assessment is appropriate, with explicit return precautions.
Triage should be based on the current presentation and expected care, with reassessment if new warning signs appear.

possibleDiagnoses: Dengue fever without current warning signs
possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Laboratory assessment and oral hydration planning would allow outpatient management with explicit warning-sign return precautions.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.

aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style with smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines, warm detailed rendering and natural realistic proportions. Match the attached reference image's painterly style. Full-body wide shot, square 1:1, 3/4 front view, centered. Show the entire person, entire blue padded clinic chair and a small plain carry-on bag with all shoes and chair legs and generous margin. Subject: a Malaysian 34-year-old man in a lightweight travel shirt and chinos. Pose: sitting slumped, one hand shielding his eyes from light, the other resting on an aching thigh. Expression: feverish, photophobic and deeply achy. Visible signs: flushed face, tired eyes and only a very faint sparse pink macular rash on the forearms; the rash must be subtle and not visually dominant. No bleeding, bruising, dramatic spots, mosquito, text, logos, shadows, floor plane, watermark or border. Perfectly flat solid #00ff00 chroma-key background.
